items.title: Warframe creator Digital Extremes is launching alpha playtests for its next game Soulframe
items.summary: Soulframe Open Preludes kick off in November 2026.
items.content:
All News Soulframe is getting an open alpha (Image: Digital Extremes).

{" "} Warframe creator Digital Extremes is launching alpha playtests for its next game Soulframe .iframe-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .img-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .a-img-media {aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} Soulframe Open Preludes kick off in November 2026. Warframe creator Digital Extremes is officially opening up early alpha playtesting for its next game, Soulframe. PC players worldwide can access the game on 6 November in what the developer calls “Soulframe Open Preludes.” This version of the game adds an Omen Wolf mount system, a new world progression system, and fishing features.

In a monthly developer livestream, Digital Extremes shared more details for the next Soulframe Preludes updates coming in November, entitled Verse of the Veilands. This update will add a bunch of new content to the game, and mark the beginning of Soulframe Open Preludes, the latter of which is an early alpha playtest for PC players worldwide.

Creative director Geoff Crookes said on the announcement:

"Soulframe has been a community-driven game from day one, shaped by the tight-knit group of players that joined us for Preludes, and now, we're ready to grow that community even further. It feels a little scary to finally open the gates like this, but the introduction of mounts and world progression systems we revealed today is the right time so we can gather essential feedback on these features and everything we've worked on so far. The more players we have right now, the more helpful it is for our team to inform the direction Soulframe takes. Thank you to everyone who has helped get us this far."

Soulframe Open Preludes is a free-to-play alpha version of the game that will be available for download on the game’s official website, and playable on Windows PC. First-time players can explore a large open world, master combat styles, and forge Pacts with animal-like Omen Beasts. This version of the game will also include story quests called Fables, as well as co-op multiplayer, crafting, and more.

Additionally, the Verse of the Veilands update will add a new environmental world progression system called Veilands, the ability to grow wolf pups into Omen Wolf mounts, a new character Pact, and the return of Bita’s Eve.

Soulframe Open Preludes will launch on 6 November, 2026.

New details have been revealed for Warframe: Tau, bringing the new Warframe Brysko, voiced by Matthew Mercer, and more this December.

Digital Extremes revealed all of the new content coming soon for Warframe: Tau , the latest expansion of the game that will cap off a pretty successful 2026 for the game. The content will arrive sometime in December 2026, but a date has not yet been set. Within it, you'll travel to a new star system, get a new Warframe with Brysko, a ton of cosmetics, and more. Plus, they will be launching a new card game based on the video game. We have the dev notes below, along with images and the recent dev video.

Venture to a new Star System, Tau, and discover a new single-player cinematic narrative chapter, unlocking new variants of cooperative gameplay modes, including a revamped Survival mission on the Fornax moon, Perita, to squad up with friends online. All for free, on all major console and PC platforms.

Step beyond the Origin System and enter a paradise lost to war and ruin. A brand-new Star Chart is filled with new forces, friends and foes, and so much to discover. The Old Peace (Dec. 2025) update introduced players to what Tau once was, and Warframe: Tau (Dec. 2026) will unearth what has become following eons of conflict, with a first look at present-day Perita and the hostile forces overseeing this decayed wasteland.

Perita will debut with Warframe: Tau in December alongside the mob-run ring city of Fornax as two distinct locations, on which players will discover new stories and challenges while Tau evolves with each following update. Take a trip down to MANIFOLD 90-BF, a new social hub on the mafia-riddled Fornax full of new characters, rivals, and lore secrets to uncover. Cut through the chaos of the Perita to encounter The Cleaving Glaive, a new ally Syndicate scavenging the Perita wasteland in search of Tau secrets.

The 67th Warframe, Brysko, will be available to all Warframe players and can be instantly unlocked from the Warframe Market or earned through gameplay when Warframe: Tau arrives in December. Voiced by legendary actor Matthew Mercer ( Final Fantasy VII: Revelation, The Legend of Vox Machina ) in a curious inner monologue, Brysko draws on the detective noir genre and serves as the protagonist of the single-player cinematic narrative Quest players will discover when Warframe: Tau arrives. Brysko leads the charge in an all-new cosmetic class in Warframe – the Chimera Skin. Players were treated to a deep dive into Brysko's ability kit and gameplay mechanics, showcasing his Hound companion, signature gear like his Rain & Shine fist weapons, and his Exalted magnum — Corecracker.

Weave the strands of destiny with the dice maiden Koumei's first-ever Deluxe Skin release, Koumei Enshoujo. A first look at Koumei's avant-garde cosmetic design was showcased live in-game ahead of her femme fatale release alongside Warframe: Tau in December. The mercurial firemonger Nezha is next in line for the Warframe Heirloom Skin treatment, with a first look at concept art revealed. Co-designed with Mati Tapia and Stephan Sotelting of Sumo Digital and Digital Extremes, players won't want to miss out on this one-of-a-kind skin arriving in early 2027.

Raise the stakes for board game night with the new Portau Card Collection and Portau Playmat, now available for pre-order from the Official Warframe Merch Store. Tune in to Digital Extremes' Princess Margaret Foundation Cancer Quest finale stream Saturday, Oct. 31 at 12 p.m. ET on Warframe's Twitch and YouTube channels to watch the team and some very special guests face off in an all-out Portau tournament.

Set in the far reaches of outer space during a new Dark Age, WarFrame introduces the Tenno, a race on the brink of extinction after being enslaved by the Grineer for centuries. Players enter WarFrame on the cusp of the Grineer's victory over the Tenno until they begin to arm themselves with WarFrames - an ancient exo-skeletal technology only they can operate. Hidden within the Orokin Derelicts of a lost civilization, new WarFrames lie dormant and undiscovered. These artifacts are the Tenno's only hope for survival.

WarFrame is a free-to-play fast-action PvE shooter set in an evolving sci-fi world. Some would call it MMO-Lite as squads of four players band together to advance their characters and battle the oppression of the genocidal Grineer. Throughout their combat missions, players will continually increase the power and abilities of their WarFrame and weapons. Players will raid new areas of space searching for exotic and powerful weapons and WarFrame augmentations to customize their arsenal. With WarFrame's Automatic Mission Generator, the game will offer endless replay as levels are procedurally configured for a unique raid -- every time.

Tau is in sight. A new era of Warframe awaits players beyond The Origin System as Digital Extremes prepares to invite those, new and returning, to discover a new Star System with Warframe: Tau in December, arriving for free on all PC, console, and mobile platforms.

To all our players, new and returning, the Origin System is not being left behind. While we focus right now on Tau, we have so many stories to tell, and now just have more places to share them.”

items.title: Warframe's fantasy-pilled sister Soulframe finally goes open to all this November, though Digital Extremes are "nervous" about certain changes
items.summary: Soulframe's open PC release and 17th prelude update are upon us, and Digital Extremes are celebrating by destroying its world to give players more direction.
items.content:
They're celebrating the end of closed alpha by poisoning the world

Image credit: Digital Extremes / Rock Paper Shotgun News by Edwin Evans-Thirlwell News Editor Published on Oct. 30, 2026, 8:30 p.m. 4 comments Follow Soulframe Warframe creators Digital Extremes have announced that their free-to-play fantasy RPG Soulframe will be available for everyone to download on 6th November, after two years in closed alpha. Finally, you serfs without "prelude" keys will be able to fire up Soulframe.com and make sense of my ranting about the sleeping animals on the lobby screen.

The new "open prelude" will land shortly before the game's 17th major update, Verse of the Veilands, which lets you grow your Omen wolfpup allies into rideable adult wolves by finding the ingredients for a special biscuit. More importantly, prelude 17 violently rearranges the game's wistful world, adding an Ubisoft-esque region purging system that is designed to guide new players a bit more emphatically towards the game's "votives". Aka, missions. Yes, Digital Extremes sort of have a bespoke term for every game feature in Soulframe. I find this can be either charming or maddening, depending on how much sleep I've had.

Here's how the region purging will work: after completing the game's Tormented Stag quest, you'll find that the landscape is being corrupted by siphons deployed by the villainous star-faring Ode faction. You have to complete votives to build energy and learn the sacred song of each region, allowing you to cleanse it and restore the environment.

In a roundtable preview session last week, creative director Geoff Crookes and lead designer Scott McGregor expressed a certain amount of anxiety about deliberately polluting Soulframe's fairytale ambience. "Scott and I were just talking yesterday about, aesthetically, how nervous we are about this change," Crookes commented, "because the game has gotten a lot of really great feedback on how cosy it is, how beautiful the world is, and you're going to enter a game that is much more unforgiving and harsh at first glance."

That said, he thinks the shift "pairs really well with going into open alpha, because it is a much stronger breadcrumb [trail] for the player, to pull them into the world and give them a bit more ownership of what they're doing." Once rinsed of Ode siphons, regions will appear more like how they are in previous versions of Soulframe, with activities such as fishing and new resources to snaffle.

McGregor added that hitherto, a lot of Soulframe players have gotten lost and put the game down after completing the opening "Fables", or story quests. "It's a really big change to the structural flow of the game, you know," he told the assembled journorabble. "We're very open and discoverable, and we had a lot of player feedback that was basically 'what do I do next? What do I do next? I don't know what to do next'.

"So [it's] taking that and mashing it with the votive system, which is our mission system for the game, and making that more of a directed experience," he went on, "and then once they get through that directed experience, they can go back to that open world." Prelude 17 will also let you accept votives more straightforwardly from the world map, after finding the local representative or mission giver.

Digital Extremes have a new Soulframe "pact" or character loadout on the boil, the Ode Shrike. It's a dastardly poacher class who specialises in spike traps and throwable bolas. The Shrike's standout ability is a balloon dart that lets you hoist enemies into the sky, as in Metal Gear Solid V .

You can read more about Soulframe's on-going reinventions on the official site . While you won't need a key to get access as of Nov 6th, the game's paid Founders program will remain the same. Digital Extremes will likely still run closed preview builds alongside the "open prelude", testing out features with a smaller group of players. They're also looking into giving you the ability to reset your character, so you can check out any new material added to parts of the game you've finished.

I'm not sure I've ever been exhilarated by Soulframe, but I like the poise, flamboyance and gentle complexity of its combat . I also really enjoy its faded tapestry aesthetics, though I think it's yanking on the goo-goo glands too avidly with all these fluffy forest animals. Enough photogenic wolfpups, Digital Extremes - let's see you make, I don't know, a blobfish look adorable.

It's also very interesting as a new live service project from a company defined by the success of Warframe. I spoke to the Soulframe developers earlier in the year about the challenge of borrowing Warframe's thunder without getting lost in its shadow .

items.summary: Verse of the Veilands will radically change the structure of the game so it
items.content:
Verse of the Veilands will radically change the structure of the game so it's easier for new players to follow.

(Image credit: Digital Extremes) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter After three years of invite-only playtests, Soulframe is opening its doors to everyone next week on November 6. If you've been waiting to see what the developers of Warframe are doing with a fantasy action RPG, you'll finally be able to jump in and see for yourself.

The transition to an open alpha will be followed by a massive transformation to the structure of the game later in November. Midrath, Soulframe's big open landmass, won't be the verdant, almost chill, place it used to be: The entire area will be corrupted and it's your job to bring it back to life. "You're going to enter a game that is much more unforgiving and harsh at first glance," creative director Geoff Crookes explained in a recent presentation attended by PC Gamer.

This update, Prelude 17 or Verse of the Veillands, is a huge shift for Soulframe, but an important one that will help new players acclimate to the world. Crookes said the goal is to improve the onboarding experience and to give players "much more ownership" over their decisions early on. It won't be fully finished yet, however, so what's in there today is just "the functional bones" of what will come in the final game.

Feedback from players who struggled to reach the point of the game where they could freely explore the open world convinced the team there needed to be a more direct intro. In Verse of the Veilands, the main quest will teach you how to stop the siphons draining the world of its color. Enemies and resources you encounter will change as each zone is restored and side activities, like fishing, will become available. You'll also be able to raise a wolf pup into a full-on mount.

"The system is also helping the worldbuilding," Crookes said. Pages and pages of new writing for each faction leader will be added and you'll start to hear them radio in and fill you in on the history of the world. The team said it wants them to have a more "integrated" role in your journey as you work to cleanse Midrath of the corruption.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different Despite the tragic death of its lead writer, one of the scariest games I have ever played will finally come out later this month The next game in a huge Chinese action RPG series has plenty of action, but I hope it hasn't totally abandoned the RPG

A new Pact, Soulframe's equivalent of a class (or a Warframe), will be added, too. The name of it was still undecided during the presentation, but the developers described it as a "hunter, poacher-type Pact" related to the alien Ode race. Equipping it will let you tie enemies together with a sci-fi bola, pierce them with a cone of spikes, and send them flying away by attaching a giant balloon to them à la Metal Gear Solid 5.

The developers stressed that there's a lot packed into Verse of the Veilands, so much so that they were still tweaking things days before the presentation. Crookes and McGregor nervously expressed that it would "hopefully" be done in time for today, but it seems it won't quite make it in time. That said, the plan is for the update to be out before the end of the next month, so new players might want to wait until then.

"I think this is probably one of the biggest, most violent changes we've made to the structure of the game in a long while," lead designer Scott McGregor said. "Paired with open Preludes is nerve-wracking and we hope players and the feedback stays positive."

items.title: Warframe Devstream 198 Breakdown
items.summary: Devstream 198 for Warframe focused on a lot of Tau, Brysko and much more. Here is everything we learned from the stream!
items.content:
The first major Devstream for the Tau update in Warframe has just wrapped up. This Devstream focused a lot on what players can expect with that update, alongside some little goodies and even a retrospective on 2026 for the game. From the scope of Tau to more Hex content and even the Portau official card game, here is everything we learned from Devstream 198!

They opened the Devstream by talking about the launch of the official Portau card game. There is going to be a play mat, two sets of cards, and even a cool keychain that can be yours if you preorder here . They will also be hosting a tournament tomorrow on their Twitch channel for charity .

From here, they went over a retrospective on Warframe in 2026. Detailing each update from Shadowgrapher to the Android and Nintendo Switch 2 launch to Iceblade of Narin , and how each of those updates was received and the lessons they learned from them. During this segment, they went over how Icebind , the new 6-player game mode, will be receiving matchmaking next year.

Following this, they talked about how players will be able to enjoy more content for the Hex, including the Captura dates added in The Old Peace . This was announced alongside the heirloom skin for Nezha (sorry, Excalibur fans) and Koumei’s Deluxe skin.

But seeing as this was a Devstream dedicated to Tau, they focused on showing a lot of exciting content for it, including its release window!

They started by announcing that Tau will be arriving in December and may be two to three hours in length for the questline. It was emphasized that this questline will be more focused on the operator, as opposed to the Drifter.

Tau is going to be a brand new solar system, and it is going to launch with two regions. Perita from The Old Peace and Fornax. The Faction for Perita will be called the Cleaving Glaive, and will be filled with old Dax Anarchists that have evolved in the time since The Old Peace. These two locations will have 6 new missions, including new ones where it is shown that there is a blinding sandstorm on Perita that players will have to venture into. This is being added alongside older mission types like Void Cascade. They also outlined that Perita will have 10 older prime warframe relic sets that you can farm to earn at your leisure, instead of relying on Varzia.

There will also be new damage types being added to Warframe with Tau. This will involve combining Slash, Puncture, or Impact with the Tau damage type for a new combination. From here, they outlined how Brysko will play, and he looks like quite the strong addition to the roster!

Brysko is the new detective-themed warframe and is also voiced by Matthew Mercer. They confirmed that his chimera variant skin will allow you to hear his voice while you play. He is going to come with, of course, a new alternate helmet and an exciting kit of abilities. Below are his passive and his abilities:

From here, they showed off a bit of Fornax, the ring around a planet on Tau. Fornax already has a unique punishment while playing in it. If you fall off a ledge, you die, not just spawn where you fell. Fornax will have 3 hubs you can venture to while you play in it. One will be the casino, and another will feature a giant sentient head with other NPCs that act as your vendors for that planet. Fornax will also feature vehicular gameplay and little grapple points to help you get around. They also detailed how Steel Path will work. There will not be acolytes, but instead little assassins sent out by the Hunra. Fornax will also feature void fissure missions. But this is all that we saw during the Devstream regarding Tau.

Devstream 198 was only 1 part of 2 Devstreams for Tau. The next is set for November 27th and will also feature the reveal of the next prime warframe (including the trailer). If you would like to watch the full Devstream for any minute details and the stunning gameplay shown, you can find it below!

items.title: Warframe: Tau Coming In December
items.summary: Your remarkable journey is about to lead to an era-defining trip to the Tau System, where new worlds ripe for exploration are waiting. Jump back into Warframe today and get ready to experience our most expansive update ever this December. 6
items.content:
Your remarkable journey is about to lead to an era-defining trip to the Tau System, where new worlds ripe for exploration are waiting. Jump back into Warframe today and get ready to experience our most expansive update ever this December.

67TH WARFRAME: BRYSKO

Hit the streets of Fornax as Brysko, the world-weary, noir-inspired detective brought to life with an inner monologue voiced by Matt Mercer. Enforce your own brand of street justice with an indomitable suite of Abilities, trusty Hound Companion and signature armaments like the Rain & Shine Fist Weapons and Corecracker Exalted Pistol. Brysko also introduces the first in a new class of premium Customizations: the Chimera Skin. As with a Protoframe, you'll be able to switch between his Warframe and Chimera aspects on the fly for a more Sentient appearance and voice-acted dialogue.

TAU STAR CHART

Your evolution continues in a new region of space beyond anything you've ever known: the Tau System. While there will remain much to do in the Origin System going forward, you'll also be able to enter Missions and explore new worlds across Tau. December will start you off with the mob-run ring city of Fornax, as well as the badlands of Perita, with many more planned for future updates.

PERITA

Although Perita thrived following the events of The Old Peace, its ecosystem has since collapsed into a hostile desert populated by feuding clans of Dazannah — and where both resources and allies are notoriously difficult to come by. With the last unconquered clan facing existential peril, its chieftain’s young son, Catulast, seeks help from its ancient foe, the Tenno. Will you brave the wasteland and answer its call?

A relentless embodiment of the Infestation, Nidus Prime thrives in the chaos of the battle, growing stronger with every mutation. Harness his parasitic powers to ensnare enemies, unleash devastating attacks and bolster his own survivability. With no conventional shields to rely on, Nidus Prime is an excellent choice for Tenno who prefer an aggressive, ability-driven playstyle that rewards you the longer you stay in the fight.

Saryn Prime

A deadly plague given form, Saryn Prime spreads toxic devastation across the battlefield, leaving few enemies untouched. Infect foes with corrosive spores, empower your weapons with lethal toxins and unleash waves of viral destruction upon entire groups. Her exceptional area-of-effect damage makes her an excellent choice for Tenno who enjoy overwhelming enemies and clearing large crowds with ease.

Prime Warframes

Check out our guide to Prime Warframes video for a helpful breakdown of what Prime Warframes are, different ways you can earn them and how you can purchase Prime items.

items.title: Warframe’s Five-Year Plan
items.summary: What it takes to keep a live-service game from dying
items.content:
In early 2022, Rebecca Ford, formerly Warframe ’s director of community and live ops, took over as creative director, marking the beginning of a new era for the then-nearly-decade-old massively multiplayer space ninja fashion simulator. Taking the reins on such an established game would’ve been a daunting prospect for anyone, even someone as intimately familiar with it as Ford. But she and her cohort came armed with a plan.

The thing about game development, though, is that it’s fraught with unforeseen wobbles and stumbles, which can presage full-on faceplants. Even the best-laid plans rarely emerge from the process unaltered. Add to that the crucial fact that Warframe is a live-service game with its own daily, weekly, and monthly wants and needs; you can never entirely predict how its sometimes-obsessively dedicated player base will react to change.

So how can developers possibly lay down track to carry the game forward for five years while still leaving wiggle room to swerve? It’s an art, a science, and a math problem all rolled into one. Now, at the tail end of her first five years at the helm, Ford can reflect with clear eyes on what panned out, as well as what didn’t.

"You have to take big swings, or you join the statistic of the percent of live-service games that fail in a given year,” Ford told Aftermath. “One live-service game failing is a tragedy; one hundred a year is a statistic, and you must strive to radiate your DNA."

Warframe has long been prone to unexpected shifts in tone, subject matter, and even genre, with the past half-decade’s expansions taking players everywhere from a demented fantasyland , to the year 1999 , to World War 1-inspired trenches . But much of what’s happening in the game today—namely, a long-awaited journey to the star system that set the game’s whole story in motion, Tau —existed on a white board in Digital Extremes’ offices back in 2022.

During our interview, Ford walked me through it, pointing to recently revealed story beats like [SPOILERS] Lotus, the player character’s beloved space mom, cutting a deal with an Eldritch space horror known as The Man In The Wall to save all the child soldiers who pilot Warframes, as well as a more prominent role for Praghasa, Lotus’ mom who is also a spaceship [END SPOILERS].

“We really had the fundamental questions that felt relevant for Warframe —which [are] ‘What is The Man In The Wall? … Did Lotus cut a deal with The Man In The Wall? And then Praghasa, what’s going on with her?’—[mapped out],” said Ford. “Some of these will be very deeply explored in the quest that you're going to play at the end of the year with Tau. You can see the process from 2022 and us continuing to refine the timeline and what we think is important.”

By 2023, the team had already sketched out the intro to Tau , which finally debuted at this year’s TennoCon in London, Ontario and featured a noir detective-inspired Warframe, Brysko, skulking through the slums of a goopy, glistening city full of drug-addicted automatons.

“We knew [back in 2023] that Tau was going to be our addict arc, where it's like a Sentient-fentanyl parallel,” said Ford. “So all roads lead to Tau, and for three years we've been working in that direction, year over year.”

Another white board from 2023 featured a full chronological timeline of key moments throughout Warframe ’s centuries-spanning saga.

“For staging everything, white boards and analog are still so much how we work,” Ford said.

Ford also uses software to create a visual plan for every year, quarter by quarter, that outlines “all the big swings,” including the themes underpinning individual Warframes that will be released. This, however, is one place where Digital Extremes has decided to zig when it was planning to zag during Ford’s tenure as creative director.

Originally, a detective Waframe, Brysko, was going to be introduced in 2025, with his mini-story serving as the player’s first strides into Tau’s seedy underbelly. But then the team decided to move all of the Tau update to 2026, necessitating a new frame for that slot in 2025. Why? Because Warframe ’s ex-stewards, who’d since moved over to alpha-stage fantasy sister game Soulframe , had a great idea for an update that would serve as a lead-in to Tau : a leap back into the distant past known as The Old Peace . This would better establish the history between players’ faction, the Tenno, and the aforementioned Sentients, enemies turned allies (tragically) turned enemies again who are now the main occupants of Tau.

“We shipped a playable Old War,” said Ford, “which was a creative moment that the old team, Steve [Sinclair] and Geoff [Crookes], were like ‘You should really do this,’ and we were like, ‘Oh, you're so right. We'll add that to the plan to make Tau more impactful.’ So [ Tau and Brysko] got pushed back a year so we could make room for this.”

items.title: Warframe director promises new Tau expansion doesn’t mean the game’s original star system won't get new content
items.summary: Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford explains that the new Tau expansion doesn't mean the original Origin system will be abandoned.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Warframe director promises new Tau expansion doesn’t mean the game’s original star system won’t get new content Published:

Digital Extreme’s free-to-play behemoth Warframe is heading outside of its initial star system and into the Tau system. While brand-new adventures await, the studio is keen to note that they are not abandoning the system players have called home for more than ten years.

Since its 2012 PC alpha, Warframe has stayed mostly within the Origin star system. Outside of missions set in The Void, the PvE MMO has remained within one system, but with the upcoming Tau expansion later this year, players will be able to jump into a brand-new system.

Right now, players can already experience the prologue to this new expansion. Prologue to Tau, a new permanent quest, released earlier this month and is still ongoing, allowing fans to narratively prepare for the new expansion. But what comes after?

In an interview with Japanese outlet Denfaminicogamer , creative director Rebecca Ford explained that the future of Warframe is not entirely set in Tau. Instead, new content will come to both systems with no intention of leaving the old star system in the dust.

“Some might wonder if heading toward the Tau system means the Origin system will be left behind or forgotten,” Ford told the outlet. “But rest assured—whether you are a new player or someone returning to the game, there is no need to worry.”

Ford explained that the arrival of the Tau system only adds to Warframe’s universe with “new possibilities for the stories we can tell and the ideas we can explore”. While Warframe never felt restricted by its adherence to a single star system, the team believes exploring outwards invites new opportunities.

The creative director explained that the arrival of Tau will also mean more content in Origin. “It does not mean we are “finished” with the Origin system,” she said. “The Origin system remains a vital part of Warframe and will continue to be a significant focus in our future development.”

After a decade-plus of support, Ford is keen to note that Warframe is not slowing anytime soon. With the death of Destiny 2, Warframe has continued to grow , and Digital Extremes is keen to continue supporting the beloved online looter-shooter for years as it works on Soulframe, which will release eventually.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

items.title: 5 Best Video Games Like Warframe
items.summary: If you dig the action in "Warframe" and are looking for something that will give you an analogous experience, check out these five games.
items.content:
Digital Extremes Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Warframe" is a video game that has stood the test of time for over a decade and continues to reward its loyal player base with fresh content, updates, and support. The game can't really be tethered to a single genre either, as it's an MMO, RPG, sci-fi-based story adventure, and looter shooter all wrapped up into a single package. While this makes the game feel accessible to a wide variety of players, it can also make it difficult for players to compare "Warframe" to any other game on offer.

Fortunately, some titles out there share one or more similarities with "Warframe" and can give you a comparable experience. While these titles might not be free-to-play and possess thousands of hours of content like "Warframe," they have at least one shared feature with the game that makes you feel like stepping into the suit of your Tenno all over again. Below, you'll find five games similar to "Warframe" and why fans might enjoy playing them.

Bungie "Destiny 2" is arguably the closest comparison to "Warframe" available in 2026. Both games are MMOs set in a sci-fi world with plenty of emphasis on developing the story. Not only that, but you'll also find that "Destiny 2" shares plenty of the same core elements as "Warframe," including collecting vast amounts of loot, selecting and customizing your character's class, and completing missions in co-op multiplayer. While it might sound like "Destiny 2" isn't anything different from "Warframe," that's not the case in the slightest, as the two play very differently, gameplay-wise.

"Destiny 2" is a fast-paced first-person shooter with a more challenging combat system that demands strategy and mastery over your weapons and skills. Raids present the most difficult challenge in the game, as these are large-scale events that reward a ton of loot, but there's plenty of individual content to take part in as well. Just like "Warframe," you can engage with this content as a solo player or in a party, and there are both PvE and PvP elements across a variety of modes and events. The two games might not play exactly the same, but "Destiny 2" is your best bet if you want something with all of the features that make "Warframe" great. However, it should be noted that developer Bungie has announced major changes to the future of "Destiny 2," which has caused a dip in player count.

Arrowhead Game Studios Compared to "Warframe," "Helldivers 2" offers a totally different experience from top to bottom. While both games have a sci-fi setting and feature co-op functionality, "Helldivers 2" doesn't really fall into any of the genres that define "Warframe." Instead, the game is a unique action-adventure experience that takes teamwork to a whole new level. "Helldivers 2" can't be played solo and requires four players to be in a party nearly at all times.

With your party, which can be comprised of friends or strangers that you match with, you'll drop into specific missions that are taking place all over a galaxy on different planets. You have various objectives you need to complete on these planets and a certain amount of time to extract before you fail the mission. When you're completing objectives, some of which are nearly impossible to finish , you can use a predefined loadout that you set before a drop starts. Your loadout can consist of weapons, gear, and special abilities that you unlock the further you progress. "Helldivers 2" is an entirely interactive and unique experience that doesn't offer the same narrative aspect as "Warframe," but its gameplay loop is highly rewarding.

NEXON "The First Descendant" is the only game on this list that primarily follows the "Warframe" model of being a free-to-play MMO looter shooter. While "The First Descendant" features far more monetization, the two games have a very similar gameplay style that "Warframe" fans will immediately recognize and be able to hop into. From the third-person perspective to the character customization to the overwhelming number of cosmetics, there's a lot to like if you're a "Warframe" fan.

Even the settings of the two games are similar, as "The First Descendant" takes place in a sci-fi universe where your character has enhanced abilities and travels to all sorts of different planets during the story. However, there's not a huge emphasis on the story, as "The First Descendant" is more about the loot grind than anything else. To obtain most rare pieces of gear, you need to research their designs, and you can do that by acquiring blueprints from various bosses and objectives. This can be a huge time commitment, though, as "The First Descendant" can have you repeating a boss for days before you get the drop you want.

Blizzard Entertainment From a strictly gameplay perspective, "Warframe" and "Diablo 4" are extremely different. One is a fast-paced third-person shooter MMO, while the other is a top-down ARPG with distinct character classes that alter your entire playstyle. However, if you take a look under the hood, "Diablo 4" has plenty to like if you're a "Warframe" fan.

For starters, "Diablo 4" places an enormous emphasis on loot, as every enemy and boss you kill has a chance to drop some rare piece of gear. While guns don't play a role in the loot, you can obtain weapons, such as staves or melee weapons, as well as jewelry and armor with certain traits that boost your character's abilities. "Diablo 4" also has an excellent base campaign filled with unique open-world zones, tough bosses, and progression. While you can also take on one of the several expansion campaigns, you can also engage in some PvP or the endgame grind that focuses on improving your loot and stats. Getting past the top-down view and alternate RPG mechanics might be hard at first for "Warframe" players, but "Diablo 4" is worth learning some new playstyles.

2K Arguably the most influential franchise in the entire looter shooter genre is "Borderlands," which helped define the genre back when the original game was released in 2009. While you could play any of the "Borderlands" games for a top-notch looter shooter experience, "Borderlands 4" is the most recent entry in the franchise. You don't need to play any of the previous games in the series to understand what's going on, either, so you can just hop right in.

Aside from the focus on looting, "Borderlands 4" and "Warframe" are both story-driven RPGs with open worlds and deep character progression. "Borderlands 4" can also be played with friends, as the series has been regarded as one of the best co-op experiences ever . However, there are more differences than similarities between the two games, as "Borderlands 4" is a first-person shooter with no PvP whatsoever. That said, the game is still an incredible experience, as you have a huge world to explore, vehicles to ride, and more loot than you'll ever know what to do with. It also features plenty of edgy dialogue and cutscenes, which often lead to some outrageous moments in both the main story and side quests. So, if you're looking for a witty and fun looter shooter RPG to hop into after a "Warframe" session, "Borderlands 4" certainly fits the bill.

items.title: "Devourer" Single Release
items.summary: The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for y
items.content:
The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for your listening pleasure on major streaming platforms. "Devourer," was first heard during the Epoch Operation: Taubound Official Gameplay Teaser. Influenced by slow, heavy metal from the likes of Black Sabbath, it features lyrics "sung" in Voidtongue, the terrifyingly enigmatic language of the Untime. This was a deliberate choice, recalling the memorable moment from 2023's Whispers in the Walls Quest when you took control of one of Albrecht Entrati's Vessels for the first time. Here, these elements combine for a musical experience that feels as massive and imposing as your latest endeavors ahead of Warframe: Tau, coming later this year.
